questions.q: Kathakali is the classical dance form of which state?
questions.e: Kathakali is the elaborate dance-drama of Kerala, known for its heavy make-up and costumes.

questions.q: Bharatanatyam is associated with
questions.e: Bharatanatyam originated in the temples of Tamil Nadu. Kuchipudi belongs to Andhra Pradesh.

questions.q: The famous Pushkar Fair, known for its camel trading, is held in
questions.e: The Pushkar Fair is held near Pushkar in Rajasthan around Kartik Purnima.

questions.q: Onam is the harvest festival of
questions.e: Onam is celebrated mainly in Kerala in the month of Chingam (August–September).

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a member of the Carnatic music trinity?
questions.e: The trinity is Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri. Purandara Dasa is called the father of Carnatic music, and he is not one of the three.

questions.q: The Taj Mahal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is located in
questions.e: The Taj Mahal at Agra, built by Shah Jahan, was inscribed in 1983.

questions.q: Madhubani painting is a folk art of
questions.e: Madhubani (Mithila) painting comes from the Mithila region of Bihar. Warli is from Maharashtra and Pattachitra from Odisha.

questions.q: Pandit Ravi Shankar was a world-famous exponent of the
questions.e: Ravi Shankar was a sitar maestro. Ustad Amjad Ali Khan plays the sarod and Bismillah Khan the shehnai.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Sattriya
I. It is a classical dance form of Assam.
II. It developed in the Vaishnavite monasteries (satras) of Assam, in the tradition of Sankardeva.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Sattriya, recognised as a classical dance in 2000, grew in the satras of Assam and is linked to Sankardeva's Vaishnavite movement.

questions.q: The Hornbill Festival is celebrated in
questions.e: The Hornbill Festival is held every December in Nagaland, near Kohima.

questions.q: Kalhana's Rajatarangini is a chronicle of the kings of
questions.e: The Rajatarangini, written in Sanskrit in the 12th century, narrates the history of Kashmir's kings.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Lotus Temple in Delhi
I. It is a Bahá'í House of Worship.
II. It was built by the Mughals in the 17th century.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Lotus Temple is a Bahá'í House of Worship completed in 1986, so it has no link with Mughal-era building.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Humayun's Tomb in Delhi
I. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
II. It was built during the reign of Akbar.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Humayun's Tomb was inscribed in 1993 and was built from about 1565 to 1572, in Akbar's reign. Both statements are correct.

questions.q: The architect of India Gate and the Viceroy's House (now Rashtrapati Bhavan) in New Delhi was
questions.e: Edwin Lutyens designed India Gate and the Viceroy's House. Herbert Baker designed the Secretariat buildings.

questions.q: The Kangra school of miniature painting developed in
questions.e: Kangra painting flourished in the Himalayan foothills of present Himachal Pradesh, with Radha–Krishna themes.

questions.q: Which of the following was NOT among the first Indian sites inscribed as World Heritage in 1983?
questions.e: The 1983 batch had Agra Fort, Taj Mahal, Ajanta and Ellora. Konark Sun Temple was inscribed in 1984.

questions.q: The Sun Temple at Konark was built in the 13th century by which Eastern Ganga ruler?
questions.e: Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty built the Konark temple in the form of a chariot of the Sun god.

questions.q: The composer who used the mudra (signature) 'Guruguha' in his compositions was
questions.e: Muthuswami Dikshitar signed his Sanskrit kritis with 'Guruguha'. Syama Sastri used 'Syama Krishna'.

questions.q: Match the work with its author.
questions.e: Kamayani is by Jaishankar Prasad, Gitagovinda by Jayadeva, Harshacharita by Banabhatta and Silappatikaram by Ilango Adigal.

questions.q: Match the festival with the state in which it is celebrated.
questions.e: Wangala is the Garo festival of Meghalaya, Chapchar Kut is Mizoram's spring festival, Losoong is Sikkim's New Year and Sarhul is a Jharkhand tribal festival.
